An Introduction to Knowledge Graphs and
Retrieval-Augmented Generation
1. Graph Databases
Neo4j is a graph database that stores information as nodes and relationships instead of tables.
Neo4j uses Cypher as its query language, which lets developers describe graph patterns directly
in a query. The Neo4j graph database also supports a native vector index, which allows it to
store both structured graph data and dense vector embeddings in a single system.
Cypher is a declarative query language developed for Neo4j. Cypher supports the MERGE
operation, which creates a node or relationship only if it does not already exist, making repeated
writes idempotent.
2. Large Language Models
Gemini is a family of large language models developed by Google. Gemini Flash is a faster,
lighter variant of Gemini optimized for high-throughput tasks such as entity extraction. Gemini
can be accessed through an API and integrated into applications using frameworks such as
LangChain.

LangChain is a Python framework that manages prompt orchestration, chaining, and integration
with external tools. LangChain provides a component called GraphCypherQAChain, which
converts a natural language question into a Cypher query and executes it against a graph
database such as Neo4j.
3. Embeddings and Entity Resolution
Sentence embeddings represent text as dense numerical vectors, allowing semantically similar
text to be compared using distance metrics. The all-MiniLM-L6-v2 model is a lightweight
sentence embedding model trained by the Sentence-Transformers project. The MiniLM model
produces 384-dimensional vectors and runs efficiently on a standard laptop CPU.
Entity resolution is the process of identifying when two different text mentions refer to the same
real-world entity. Cosine similarity is commonly used to compare embeddings during entity

real-world entity. Cosine similarity is commonly used to compare embeddings during entity
resolution, since it measures the angle between two vectors rather than their magnitude.
4. Retrieval-Augmented Generation
Retrieval-Augmented Generation, commonly abbreviated as RAG, combines information
retrieval with text generation. A RAG system retrieves relevant context before asking a language
model to generate an answer, which reduces hallucination compared to using a language model
alone.
GraphRAG extends traditional RAG by retrieving information from a knowledge graph instead of,
or in addition to, plain text passages. Hybrid retrieval systems combine graph-based retrieval
with vector-based semantic search to improve answer accuracy.
5. Application Framework and Visualization
FastAPI is a Python web framework used to build APIs. FastAPI is built on top of Starlette and

D3.js is a JavaScript library used for creating interactive data visualizations in a web browser.
D3.js is commonly used to render force-directed graphs, which are well suited for displaying
entities and relationships extracted from a knowledge graph.
pdfplumber is a Python library used to extract text and tables from PDF documents. pdfplumber
preserves page layout information, which makes it well suited for processing technical
documents that contain tables.
6. Summary
A modern knowledge graph platform typically combines several components: a document parser
such as pdfplumber, a large language model such as Gemini for entity extraction, an embedding
model such as all-MiniLM-L6-v2 for entity resolution, a graph database such as Neo4j for
